page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-4 is a general-purpose server instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16 GB of system memory. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B45 processor, the instance allocates 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU configuration includes a cache hierarchy of 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside cryptography extensions like AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the n4d-standard-4 demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance, as evidenced by its stress-ng single-core score of 3452.38 and Geekbench single-core score of 2519.0. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also rank in the top tier. Multi-core performance is average, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 5733.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 9114.6. Memory performance is mixed: cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 418.9 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block read bandwidth is weak at 37.73 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the n4d-standard-4 lies in its memory subsystem and multi-threaded scaling under heavy data loads, with weak performance in uncached large-block reads and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Database operations also show weakness, with a PassMark database score of 2596.66. Qualitatively, the instance offers balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. It is suitable for web serving, software compilation, text processing, and light-to-medium single-threaded computational tasks.
